title: AI’s Electricity Bill
status: Picks approved (all A) · waiting for the voice take · no MP4 rendered

captions.text:
Every answer AI gives you
runs on electricity.

Data centres used to
just store things.

But now they think —
and thinking takes power.

Last year, data centres used
485 terawatt-hours.

By 2030: almost double — about
3% of the world’s electricity.

So the next limit on AI may not
be chips… but power.

Who gets the power —
and who pays the bill?

iea.title: IEA, Key Questions on Energy and AI (2026): data centres 485 TWh (2025) → ~950 TWh (2030), ~3% of global electricity; AI-focused use triples
